```
DataValue_clear
clear_noInit
DataValue_clear
```

So the outer DataValue_clear is called, which calls Variant_clear on p->value. The variant contains data that is a type which has members cleared by clear_noInit. One of those members is itself a DataValue, and clearing that inner DataValue causes a use-after-free.

Let me look more carefully at DataValue_clear:
```c
static void
DataValue_clear(UA_DataValue *p, const UA_DataType *_) {
    Variant_clear(&p->value, NULL);
}
```

And Variant_clear:
```c
Variant_clear(UA_Variant *p, const UA_DataType *_) {
    if(p->storageType != UA_VARIANT_DATA)
        return;
    if(p->type && p->data > UA_EMPTY_ARRAY_SENTINEL) {
        if(p->arrayLength == 0)
            p->arrayLength = 1;
        UA_Array_delete(p->data, p->arrayLength, p->type);
    }
    if((void*)p->arrayDimensions > UA_EMPTY_ARRAY_SENTINEL)
        UA_free(p->arrayDimensions);
}
```

So Variant_clear calls UA_Array_delete on p->data. UA_Array_delete will iterate over the array elements and call clear_noInit on each. If one of the array elements (or the type itself) is a DataValue, that would call DataValue_clear again.

The issue is that DataValue_clear ONLY clears the variant (the `value` field). It does NOT clear other fields like `status` etc. But the key issue is likely that the DataValue type definition includes members that the clear_noInit function needs to handle properly.

DataValue_clear(UA_DataValue *p, const UA_DataType *_) {

```

It only clears the `value` (Variant) member. But the DataValue structure also has a `status` field and potentially other things. The issue is: when a Variant contains a DataValue (or an array of DataValues), freeing the variant's data will call DataValue_clear on each element. But if the Variant inside the DataValue *also* contains DataValues that share/reference the same data, we get a use-after-free.
